entries: Table games and services｜Dealing and determination｜At the table, verify the table and chips and equipment, dispense the correct number of cards or dice to players according to the specific game rules or operate other gambling equipment, compare the house hand with the players' hands to determine the winner, and pay out or collect chips according to the rules.

Wager acceptance and payout｜Book writing and running｜Post betting information, receive and verify and record customer wagers, scan and process winning tickets, calculate the amount due and handle the payout or refer the customer to the cage.

Residual class｜Scope and adjacent interfaces｜39-3019 provides no occupational elements, and dealing or cage tasks are not added based on the title; 43-3041 handles financial affairs, and referrals may connect but it is not included in the parent group's three-class statistics.

Compliance and identity｜Age band and restricted status and stakes｜Verify the customer's age band and restricted or self-excluded status and stake limits and identity according to jurisdictional and employer procedures, and when in doubt do not open the table or transact and escalate.

Bookkeeping and vouchers and records｜Traceability｜Keep bookkeeping and wager vouchers and winning tickets and the cash drawer and handover and log records traceable, verifying transaction by transaction and reviewing as the institution requires.

Anomalies and collaboration and reporting｜Stop and escalate｜Identify and report suspected cheating or anomalies and suspicious activity and doubtful vouchers and shortages or overages or duplicate payouts, protect customer and employee information, and refer to the supervisor and surveillance and compliance positions according to the process.

Contact intensity｜Continuous contact with others (dealer reference value 87% continuous contact); physical proximity “very close (near touching)” (dealer reference value 59%) and “moderately close (within arm's reach)” (33%).
Team and collaboration｜Working with a work group or team extremely important (dealer reference value 65% and very important 21%); coordinating or leading others important (dealer reference value 36% important, 26% extremely important).

Precision and consequences｜Must be very precise or highly accurate “extremely important” (74%) and “very important” (16%); consequences of error “extremely serious” (14%) and “serious” (15%) and “fairly serious” (36%), “not at all serious” (25%).

Customers and pressure｜Need to deal with unpleasant or angry or impolite people every day (dealer reference value 58% every day); daily need for public announcing (41% every day, 48% never); competition level “extremely competitive” (33%) and “highly competitive” (15%) and “moderately competitive” (29%).
Physical and pace｜Continuous or almost continuous standing (dealer reference value 65%) or more than half the time (27%); continuous or almost continuous use of hands to operate and control and sense objects and tools and controls (83%); continuous or almost continuous repetitive motions (70%); seated time “never” (53%) and “less than half” (28%).

subject.summary:
This page follows the U.S. SOC39-3010 statistical group, which contains only three sub-occupations: 39-3011 dealers, 39-3012 gambling and sports book writers and runners, and 39-3019 other gaming service workers. Cage workers 43-3041 is an adjacent financial affairs position and is not included in this group; managers 11-9071, first-line supervisors 39-1013, and surveillance investigators 33-9031 are also not included. The same-named OOH topic also includes managers and first-line supervisors, and its five-occupation total of 146,500 people, median of 37,460 USD, and average annual openings of 20,200 cannot be applied to the three-occupation group on this page.
Dealers operate table games, deal cards or operate equipment, compare winners, and pay out or collect money and chips; book writers and runners post information, verify and record wagers, process winning tickets, and calculate payouts or refer to the cage. 39-3019 captures only gaming services not separately listed, and O*NET does not provide occupational elements for that All Other title, so it cannot be filled in as dealing or cage work.
